depth.h2: What Algonquin Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: The median home in Algonquin was built in 1994, and more than half went up between 1990 and 2009. Most homes here aren’t old, but they’re old enough that original equipment is wearing out. Add well water and the Fox River, and the same few problems keep showing up.

tiles.title: 1990s and 2000s Homes, Original Equipment
tiles.body: More than half of Algonquin homes went up between 1990 and 2009. Equipment that came with the house, like the first water heater and the first sump pump, isn’t built to last 20 or 30 years. If yours is original, or you don’t know how old it is, have it checked before it fails. A [water heater that leaks or runs out too fast](/algonquin/water-heater-repair) is usually the first to go.

tiles.title: Living Near the Fox River
tiles.body: The Fox River runs right through Algonquin. In April 2013 it reached a record crest here, and in July 2017 volunteers filled more than 25,000 sandbags as the river rose again and some residents got water in their basements. A [sump pump with a battery backup](/algonquin/sump-pumps) keeps running when the power goes out, and a [backflow valve](/algonquin/flood-control-maintenance) stops sewage from coming up through floor drains.

tiles.title: Well Water, Testing and Filtration
tiles.body: Algonquin’s water comes from village wells on both sides of the Fox River, not from Lake Michigan. Groundwater carries minerals that can leave scale on faucets and sediment in your water heater over time. A [water test](/algonquin/water-filtration-systems) shows what’s in your water, and a filtration system can cut down on buildup.

tiles.title: Roots, Drains and Sewer Lines
tiles.body: Many of the trees planted when Algonquin’s subdivisions went in are now 17 to 36 years old, and their roots go looking for water in sewer lines. Slow drains, gurgling toilets and backups in the basement floor drain are the early signs. A [camera inspection](/algonquin/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows what’s in the line, and [hydro jetting](/algonquin/hydro-jetting) clears it out.

items.q: How much does a plumber cost in Algonquin?
items.a: It depends on the job. The main factors are what’s wrong, how hard it is to reach, the parts or materials needed and the age of your plumbing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in. Give us a call and we’ll walk you through it.

items.q: How fast can you get to my home in an emergency?
items.preview: Call us any time, day or night, including weekends and holidays.
items.a: Call us any time, day or night, including weekends and holidays. Our Esplanade Drive office keeps our plumbers close to Algonquin, and we [treat emergencies as a priority](/algonquin/emergency-plumbing). Arrival times depend on the day, but we’ll get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.preview: Algonquin’s water comes from village wells, and groundwater naturally carries minerals.
items.a: Algonquin’s water comes from village wells, and groundwater naturally carries minerals. Over time those minerals can leave scale on faucets and showerheads and sediment in your water heater. A [water test](/algonquin/water-filtration-systems) tells you exactly what’s in your water, so you know whether filtration or a softener makes sense for your home.

items.q: My home was built in the 1990s or 2000s. What should I check first?
items.preview: Start with the equipment that has a shelf life: the water heater and the sump pump.
items.a: Start with the equipment that has a shelf life: the water heater and the sump pump. If either is original to the house, it’s living on borrowed time. A camera look at your sewer line is worth it too, since roots from maturing trees are a common cause of backups. A [whole-home checkup](/algonquin/plumbing-maintenance) covers all of it in one visit.

items.q: How do I keep my basement dry when the Fox River rises?
items.preview: Make sure your sump pump works before the rain starts: pour a bucket of water into the pit and watch it turn on.
items.a: Make sure your sump pump works before the rain starts: pour a bucket of water into the pit and watch it turn on. Add a battery backup so it keeps running if the power goes out, and keep the discharge line clear and pointed away from the house. If water comes up through a floor drain instead, a backflow valve stops sewage from backing up into the basement. We can check your setup and tell you what it needs.

items.q: When should I replace my water heater?
items.preview: Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years.
items.a: Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years. Rusty water, rumbling noises, a leak at the base or hot water that runs out faster than it used to all mean it’s time to have it checked. [Replacing it](/algonquin/water-heater-installation) on your schedule is easier than dealing with a flooded basement.
